name: Beige Brown
lede: Beige Brown is a mid, warm brown with a hint of sand, a name used in several color standards.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The library lists Beige Brown in four systems: Ridgway's 1912 standard (plate XV), ISCC-NBS blocks 58 and 80, a RAL value of 8024 (a screen approximation), and Maerz and Paul, which first recorded it in 1835 on plate 7 A 12 [1]. The nearest near-duplicate is Mars Brown, at a distance of 1.8 [1].

Pastoureau notes that in the eighteenth century the half-tones, including beiges, browns, pinks and grays, multiplied as dyeing advanced and the vocabulary grew to name them [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Beige Brown appears in 13.83% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, as photographed [3]. It is more common than 94% of the named colors and peaks in the 1300s, in 17.9% of that century's 251 paintings [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone, in 28% of cases [3]. Maarten van Heemskerck is its most devoted painter here, with 7 of 12 works [3].
